claim: Roots navigate through soil integrating environmental signals to orient their growth.
source: Roots navigate through soil integrating environmental signals to orient their growth.

claim: Horizontal sample position and continuous root tip displacement present significant difficulties for live imaging.
source: Live imaging greatly aids these efforts, but the horizontal sample position and continuous root tip displacement present significant difficulties.

claim: The authors developed a confocal microscope setup for vertical sample mounting and integrated directional illumination.
source: Here, we develop a confocal microscope setup for vertical sample mounting and integrated directional illumination.

claim: TipTracker is a custom software for automatic tracking of diverse moving objects usable on various microscope setups.
source: We present TipTracker – a custom software for automatic tracking of diverse moving objects usable on various microscope setups.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the software developed, with demonstrations provided in the manuscript.

claim: The system enables observation of root tips growing along the natural gravity vector over prolonged periods of time.
source: Combined, this enables observation of root tips growing along the natural gravity vector over prolonged periods of time, as well as the ability to induce rapid gravity or light stimulation.
evidence: This is supported by experimental demonstrations in the manuscript showing multi-day imaging experiments.

claim: The system enables the ability to induce rapid gravity or light stimulation.
source: Combined, this enables observation of root tips growing along the natural gravity vector over prolonged periods of time, as well as the ability to induce rapid gravity or light stimulation.
evidence: This is supported by the rotation stage design and gravistimulation experiments described.

claim: The authors tracked migrating cells in the developing zebrafish embryo, demonstrating the utility of this system.
source: We also track migrating cells in the developing zebrafish embryo, demonstrating the utility of this system in the acquisition of high-resolution data sets of dynamic samples.

claim: Root movement is propelled by cell division and elongation.
source: Their movement is propelled by cell division and elongation (Beemster and Baskin, 1998).

claim: The temporal scale of root developmental processes ranges from minutes to days.
source: The temporal scale of these processes ranges from minutes (e.g. response to gravity) to hours (e.g. cell divisions) and days for cell differentiation (e.g. columella cell maturation).
evidence: This is based on established knowledge of plant developmental timescales.

claim: Roots of 4–5 days-old plants grow up to 300 micrometers per hour.
source: While the roots of 4–5 days-old plants grow up to 300 micrometers per hour (see below and Beemster et al., 2002)

claim: Cytokinesis and cell plate formation require approximately 30 min.
